text:
incident-bot: ALERT — production: /v1/generate p99 > 4.5s and 5xx spike detected (5m). Priority: P1. See: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/latency/overview

Maggie L: oncall here. Paging eng-runtime + platform. @Sam T @Lijuan C please triage recent rollouts and runtime pool health. :rotating_light:

Sam T: quick glance — a regional surge of 502/504 from the edge. Traces show long queue_time and many runtime-client errors: 
```
2026-03-15T12:25:12Z runtime-client error: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T12:25:13Z runtime-request queued waiting > 3s
2026-03-15T12:25:13Z gateway 502 upstream returned invalid resp
```

Lijuan C: recent push 2026-03-15-def456 at 12:18 UTC. It included a new attention kernel selector and a tweak to async kvcache eviction thresholds. Canary passed small traffic but I see a canary->prod config promotion at 12:20 that might have flipped feature flags.

Ben R: metric snapshot: p95 jumped from 200ms -> 900ms, p99 ~ 4.9s. 5xx rose to 3.4% at peak. Error budget alert fired at 12:24.

Sam T: reproducing stack: long syscall time on runtime hosts handling large context requests. Kernel CPU saturates, connections pile up. Also a surge in `kvcache.miss` events.

Maggie L: mitigation plan: 1) stop rollout / roll back release, 2) enable fallback routing to older model for requests with long context, 3) activate circuit-breaker on gateway for backend timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking. Execute in that order?

Lijuan C: rolling rollback now. @deploy-bot rollback 2026-03-15-def456.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by Lijuan C for release 2026-03-15-def456. Steps: stop canary traffic -> revert feature flags -> redeploy stable. Estimated 180s.

Sam T: I'll flip the router fallback and lower kv eviction aggressiveness temporarily. Applying gateway circuit-breaker 3500ms.

Maggie L: please also enable short-circuit caching for repeated prefixes to cut backend hits. Add temporary 5s low-latency cache for /v1/generate prefixes seen > 3x in 30s.

Sam T: router changes done: 
- fallback -> model=redwood-stable for context > 1024
- gateway circuit-breaker timeout=3500ms, fail-open=false
- transient prefix cache enabled

observability-bot: Post-mitigation metrics: 2m after rollback start — p99 down from 4.9s -> 1.1s, 5xx down to 0.8%. Latency heatmap: reduced tail in affected region.

Lijuan C: rollback finished at 12:28:55 UTC. Stable release restored. Noted that a canary config push accidentally included `kernel_selector=auto` in prod due to a templating bug.

Ben R: rough customer impact window: 12:23:45 — 12:29:10 UTC (~5m25s). Estimated ~2.7% of requests got 5xx. A few enterprise tenants saw rate-limited anomalies, support is being looped in.

Maggie L: good catch. Sam, Ben, capture one representative bad trace and one healthy trace and upload to the ticket. Also capture host-level `top` and `dmesg` around peaks.

Sam T: uploaded traces to INC-2026-1770 and pinned diffs. Bad trace shows queueing in runtime-proxy and syscalls stuck in `futex_wait` during kernel heavy path. Good trace shows no futex waits.

Lijuan C: root cause hypothesis: `kernel_selector=auto` picked an experimental fast-path that performs poorly under high P99 context and caused CPU microstalls + cache churn. The flag should have remained gated. Canary config promotion logic allowed the flag to propagate.

Ben R: customer comms draft ready for review. We'll note transient latency and rollback, include timeline and mitigation steps.

Maggie L: immediate action items:
- Lijuan C: create PR to fix templating bug and add a CI check to assert feature-flag parity between canary and prod.
- Sam T: add synthetic regression that exercises the kernel selector under high long-context load and add to pre-deploy checks.
- Ben R: finalize support comms and notify affected enterprise accounts.

Lijuan C: created ticket and PR #PR-1892, will block auto-promotion until parity checks added.

Sam T: started a stress reproducer and added it to the nightly canary suite.

observability-bot: Final stabilization snapshot at 12:36 UTC: p99=190ms, p95=160ms, 5xx=0.09%.

Maggie L: handing to post-incident owners. Postmortem ETA 72h, include timeline, feature-flag templating fix, and extra canary parity checks. I'll remain available for questions. Thanks team. :hugging_face:

Ben R: escalating to acct mgmt for any high-touch follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by Maggie L. Duration: 00:12:05. Severity: P1 -> Resolved. Report queued: https://incidents.redwood/internal/1769877000
